Coach's note, under-17 hockey, Friday
Baljeet has been different for three weeks. He arrives yawning, skips breakfast in the mess and is short with everyone. On Tuesday he argued with the referee in a practice game and walked off the field. His roommate told me he studies and scrolls until two most nights. Today I sat with him in the stands. He said he feels flat and angry and doesn't know why. We agreed on a plan: phone in the warden's box at eleven, breakfast before drills, and he can skip early practice twice this week to catch up on sleep. I'll check in with him on Monday and let his parents know how the week goes.
– Lokesh

passage:
Thursday, 11.40 pm
Four nights in a row I was up past two playing online chess. Tonight I'm writing this instead, because today was bad.
Morning: skipped breakfast, too sleepy. Maths: Siddharth asked for my ruler and I said, "Buy your own," loudly, in front of everyone. He looked at me like I was a stranger.
Lab: Sir asked me to redo my readings and I said, "I don't care," and walked out. I have never done that. I got a note for Papa to sign. He'll say, 'What happened to my good boy?'
Evening: I felt low, like everything was pointless, and ate two packets of chips for dinner.
The weird part is I wasn't even angry at them. I was just tired and empty.
New rule, my own: phone goes in the kitchen at eleven. Proper dinner. Tomorrow I say sorry to Siddharth and to Sir.
Manoj

qa.q: What did Manoj say to Sir in the lab?
qa.a: He said, "I don't care," and walked out.

qa.q: What does Manoj mean when he writes he wasn't really angry at anyone?
qa.a: He realises his snapping came from being tired and empty after nights of little sleep, not from anything Siddharth or Sir did.

qa.q: What turning point does Manoj reach, and what does he choose?
qa.a: Writing the day down makes him see the pattern, so he chooses to keep his phone in the kitchen at eleven, eat a proper dinner and apologise.

qa.q: How might Siddharth have felt when Manoj said, 'Buy your own'?
qa.a: Siddharth probably felt hurt and embarrassed in front of everyone, confused by a friend who suddenly seemed like a stranger.

grounding: It shows a teenager who stays up late every night, becomes irritable, impulsive and low, and sees that sleep and regular meals would protect his mood and choices.
